chunks: Thus he made light (of the matter) to his people, and they obeyed him. They were certainly wicked.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when Allah says 'he made light to his people' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia tafsir, this verse is frequently linked to Qarun (Korah), whose wealth and charisma led the Israelites to follow him, illustrating how material allure can corrupt a community prone to transgression. The phrase 'fasiqin' (wicked/deviant) underscores their internal moral decay, making them susceptible to external deception by a leader who exploited their desire for worldly gain.
